title: Grateful Dead Live at War Memorial on 1973-03-31
lineage: Reel master > cassette > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of an energetic show highlighted by a smoking "I Know You Rider" out of Space and powerful Jerry riffs.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean sound‑board source with the mix praised for Keith’s piano presence and overall clarity. The concert itself is high‑energy, featuring standout moments like a soaring "He's Gone," an unexpected "I Know You Rider" emerging from the Space segment, and relentless Jerry guitar work throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: One detailed 5‑star review praises both performance (high energy, many standout songs) and recording quality (clear mix), indicating an exceptional show with excellent soundboard capture.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear and balanced mix; keyboards noted as nicely audible; no complaints of drop‑outs or muddiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Mellow, melodic first set leads into a high‑octane second set with seamless transitions—promised/bertha/greatest suite, extended jams, and an unexpected rider out of Space.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Riffs hard all night, especially on "El Paso" and the closing "Sugar Magnolia" licks; his guitar is loud and fiery.
band_member_comments.Phil: Delivers strong bass lines and baritone vocals on "He's Gone," noted as a solid backbone throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux’s piano/keys are nicely mixed, adding soulful texture to the performance.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann gets a brief 1:33 drum feature; overall rhythmic support is solid.
